title: Equivariant marked split nodal tower
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and $S\subset T$ a closed set, $G$ a group, and $d\in\mathbf N$ (including $d=0$). A marked split nodal tower of length $d$ over $(T,S)$ consists of schemes $Y_0,\ldots,Y_d$, an isomorphism $Y_0\simeq T$, morphisms $f_i:Y_i\to Y_{i-1}$, and their compatible composite maps to $T$. Every $Y_i$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Each $f_i$ is projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] (hence of finite presentation by projectivity). Its geometric fibres are connected and reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension], and each point is smooth or an ordinary double point with completed ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, using the ordinary-double-point notion of [def-trf-projective-nodal-tower]. Each residue-field fibre component with its reduced induced closed structure is smooth and geometrically irreducible over the base residue field; each nonsmooth fibre point is rational over that field. Smooth components imply that the two branches at a node belong to distinct components and are rational as well. Smoothness means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fibres are actual scheme fibre products [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For each $i$ give finitely many disjoint sections $\sigma_{ij}$ in the relative smooth locus. Give closed boundary sets $B_0=S$ under the base isomorphism and $B_i=f_i^{-1}B_{i-1}\cup\bigcup_j\sigma_{ij}(Y_{i-1})$, and require $f_i$ smooth over $Y_{i-1}\setminus B_{i-1}$. Give $G$-actions on all levels making every $f_i$ equivariant and preserving each union of sections. The stabilizer of every base point must fix individually every component, node and marked point of its fibre. Since the components are smooth and geometrically irreducible and the nodes rational, this is exactly triviality on the geometric fibre dual graph, including both ends of every edge and all marked legs. The action on $T$ is the action on $Y_0$ transported along the specified isomorphism; it need not be trivial.
